newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA GRATEFUL FOR GOALKEEPING ERROR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA GRATEFUL FOR GOALKEEPING ERROR.

text.p: A mistake by veteran international goalkeeper Andoni Zubizarreta helped Barcelona salvage a point from a thrilling Mediterranean derby with Valencia on Sunday,
Zubizarreta had denied his former team mates with a series of fine saves after Leandro had put Valencia ahead in the 42nd minute.
But he was at fault midway through the second half when he allowed a cross from Hristo Stoichkov to sail over his head, and the unmarked Ronaldo had no problems tapping in the equaliser.
The Brazilian's 24th goal of the season made up for several chances missed earlier in the game, two of them after he had broken through in a frantic opening five minutes.
Zubizarreta did well to stop one of those efforts, but as Valencia found their feet it was Barcelona keeper Vitor Baia who felt the pressure.
Portuguese international Baia had been flown in for the game in a specially-hired plane straight from Saturday's World Cup qualifier with Northern Ireland in Belfast.
He was kept on his toes and showed none of the sluggishness that had affected him the last time he had juggled club and international commitments.
Baia twice stopped efforts from winger Claudio Lopez, but could do nothing to prevent Leandro heading home Xabier Eskurza's cross from the left just before halftime.
Valencia went close to a second right after the break when Jorge Otero found Gabriel Moya unmarked on the left, and the former Sevilla striker forced a fine save out of Baia.

Although Valencia continued to look dangerous on the break it was Barcelona who took control in the second half, as Giovanni combined well with fellow midfielder Ivan de la Pena to create danger down the flanks.
Ronaldo's 70th minute goal came after Stoichkov found space down the left, and was able to clear a badly-positioned Zubizarreta.
"It was more or less fair, it was a great game," said Barcelona coach Bobby Robson.
"Because we're nine points behind Madrid people think it's a disappointing result, but as an isolated result it's good. Valencia is always a difficult game."
He rejected criticism of Ronaldo, who may have been affected by a slight leg injury.

"I think the chances came very early," said the manager. "It's very difficult to take a chance in the first two minutes and it can affect your confidence. So it was important for him to score in the second half.
"Ronaldo is 20 and he's playing all the games, all the time. He got a goal, and was in a position to get others, and in that respect I'm happy," he added.
Valencia coach Jorge Valdano said his injury-hit squad had not been equal to the demands of the second half, but agreed that the result was fair.
Valdano said he had successfully disrupted the creativity of Barcelona playmaker Josep Guardiola, while acknowledging that he was not always happy at stopping skilful opponents
"Watching players like Guardiola gives me great aesthetic pleasure," said the former Argentine international.

Valencia: 1-Andoni Zubizarreta, 3-Jorge Otero (6-Gaizka Mendieta 75), 8-Gabriel Moya, 9-Leandro, 12-Ivan Campo, 14-Jose Ignacio, 15-Francisco Ferreira, 16-Claudio Lopez (22-Jose Galvez 75), 20-Xabier Eskurza (17-Inaki Hurtado 68), 23-Vicente Engonga, 24-Fernando Caceres.

Barcelona: 1-Vitor Baia, 2-Albert Ferrer, 4-Josep Guardiola, 8-Hristo Stoichkov (17-Emmanuel Amunike 85), 9-Ronaldo, 10-Giovanni (16-Oscar Garcia 85h), 15-Laurent Blanc, 18-Guillermo Amor (19-Juan Pizzi 60), 20-Miguel Angel Nadal, 23-Ivan de la Pena, 27-Roger Garcia.
